M6 Slice 19 — the gate that could not pass.

bash
tar -xzf m6-slice-19-gate-scope.tar.gz -C /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
bash scripts/check_tree.sh
Files to DELETE: none. Five existing files replaced in place. No new file, no migration, no .csproj, no .slnx, no Program.cs.

What your run actually showed
Everything was green — dotnet build clean, dotnet test 996 / 0 failed / 981 / 15 skipped, MYRESTAURANT_E2E=1 15 passed, 0 skipped (the whole §16.3 matrix), smoke, containers, tunnel, no outdated packages. The one failure was ci_local.sh --with-all → tree hygiene FAILED: 1321 problem(s), at gate 1, so the four gates behind it never ran. CI's tree job is red for the same reason.

The only thing wrong with the repository was the gate inspecting it. The 1321 resolve exactly:

Count	Files	What was true
638 + 638	docs/llm/dump.txt, vendor/claude-output.txt	context dumps — the separator is their structure
45	every .tar.gz/.zip in docs/llm/vendor/	a gzip stream ends where it ends; a trailing 0x0A corrupts it
Two independent bugs. Gate 1 exempted export.sh but not docs/llm/, the directory export.sh writes separators into and already excludes from its own output — exempting the producer and not the product was half a rule. Separately, gates 1 and 2 were binary-safe only by accident (grep -I declines to match in binary); gate 3's tail -c 1 | wc -l had no such notion, so it accused every intact archive of being truncated.

The fix isn't a third guard — it's one predicate, is_authored_text, that all three gates consult, so they can't disagree about a file. Binary-ness is asked of grep -I rather than an extension list, which would have been wrong about the .zip files the day they landed.

What I verified
The pass matters less than the sensitivity, since a gate that passes by skipping everything is worthless. I rebuilt docs/llm/ at its real shape and confirmed the gate goes green with 17 skips — then re-introduced all five damage patterns outside it plus a CRLF, a stripped final newline, and a binary file. It reported 8 problems, named each by file and line (including Directory.Build.props:85 from gate 1 and gate 4), exited 1, and reported the binary file as 1 binary rather than accusing it.

I also compared all 310 files against yours: 305 byte-identical, and the 5 in the archive are the only ones that differ.

docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md is the complete 421 KB file, not a docs/_append/ block with a cat >> line — that was the last of those, and there's nothing left in docs/_append/ to merge.

One thing to expect: ci_local.sh --with-all will now run gates 2–5 for the first time ever under that script. If there's a surprise in this delivery, it surfaces there rather than in gate 1.
